factory.each_repetition: one retained IData release, one successful retry, high-water one at capacity one, one deferred pruning decision, two acknowledged worker replica deletions, exact oracle

rejected_results: The first combined capacity run was timing-dependent and sometimes observed no backpressure; its release window was rejected and made deterministic.
The first bounded implementation counted pending releases by scanning active transfers on a scheduling hot path; it was rejected and replaced by an exact O(1) counter.
A capacity-full volatile IData must not fall back to a stable URL that does not exist; missing IData preparation now backpressures while stable EData may still use its origin.
The overlap is described as a completed real peer byte transfer whose Controller source lease remains active after release failure; it is not misreported as bytes still in flight.
remaining_critical_work: Interrupt a positive-byte peer transfer while its source lease participates in the same pruning continuation schedule.
Invalidate the pruning proof by dynamically registering a consumer during that exact transfer window.
Exercise a real Controller release timeout rather than only deterministic pre-request failure injection.
Complete Controller restart, scale, comparison modes, and the Grand Challenge.
